all_pathways.equity_flag: The higher prevalence of anaemia in the North-West zone  may be attributed to a combination of lower socioeconomic status, limited  access to healthcare facilities, and cultural factors that inhibit parity  reduction.

all_pathways.pathway: In the North-West zone of Nigeria, unimproved water  sources contribute to increased risk of waterborne diseases, leading to  low parity and subsequently anaemia. This is compounded by poor  sanitation, husband-controlled health decisions, and lower female  education levels.
all_pathways.policy: Improve access to clean water, sanitation, and  education for women in rural areas of North-West Nigeria to reduce the  prevalence of anaemia.
all_pathways.equity_flag: Anaemia is more prevalent in the poorest segments of the  population in the North-West zone compared to other zones in Nigeria due  to socio-economic disparities and limited healthcare facilities.
all_pathways.beyond_poverty: Cultural dietary practices or limited access  to healthcare facilities may explain the pattern across different wealth  quintiles in various zones.

dominant_pathway.policy: Improved access to clean water and sanitation  facilities, family planning education, and maternal healthcare services  should be prioritized in the South-South zone.
